statements.text: We must cut carbon emissions faster through a nationwide carbon tax.
Nuclear power should be expanded to replace coal plants quickly.
We must cut carbon emissions faster through a nationwide carbon tax.
Climate policy should prioritize protecting low-income communities first.
Cities should invest heavily in free public bus and train service.
Congestion pricing in downtown areas would fund better transit systems.
Bike lanes are more cost-effective than new subway lines for most cities.
Rural areas need better transit options, not just big cities.
Zoning reform is the fastest way to make housing affordable again.
Rent control protects tenants but discourages new housing construction.
The government should build more public housing directly.
Housing subsidies should target first-time homebuyers specifically.
Carbon capture technology is not ready to replace emission cuts.
High-speed rail between major cities would reduce short-haul flights.
Short-term rental restrictions would free up housing for long-term residents.
International climate agreements need real enforcement mechanisms to work.
A revenue-neutral carbon fee returned as dividends would win public support.
Carbon taxes hit rural drivers hardest and need targeted rebates.
Emissions trading schemes have failed to raise prices high enough to matter.
Border carbon adjustments are needed so domestic industry stays competitive.
Fossil fuel subsidies should be abolished before any new carbon tax is added.
Small modular reactors could decarbonise the grid faster than wind alone.
Nuclear waste storage remains unsolved and rules out new reactor builds.
Existing nuclear plants should have their licences extended rather than closed.
Nuclear construction costs overrun so badly that renewables are the safer bet.
A stable nuclear baseload makes intermittent renewables workable at scale.
Rooftop solar subsidies mostly benefit households that are already wealthy.
Offshore wind is now the cheapest new generation we can build.
Grid-scale battery storage deserves more public investment than new generation.
Permitting reform matters more for renewables than additional subsidies do.
Transmission lines between regions are the real bottleneck for clean power.
Coastal cities should start planned retreat instead of building higher sea walls.
Flood insurance schemes encourage rebuilding in places that will flood again.
Adaptation funding for poorer countries is a moral obligation, not charity.
Urban tree planting is the cheapest way to cut deadly heat in cities.
Building codes must be rewritten now for the climate of 2070, not 1990.
Dedicated bus lanes deliver more riders per euro than any rail project.
Bus networks should be redesigned around frequency, not coverage.
Free bus fares for students and pensioners pay for themselves in ridership.
Electric buses are worth the premium purely for the air quality gains.
Rural bus routes cannot be judged by fare recovery alone.
Regional rail deserves funding long before another high-speed showcase line.
Night trains should be revived as a real alternative to short-haul flying.
Rail freight investment does more for emissions than passenger upgrades.
Metro extensions into suburbs are how you actually cut car dependency.
Station accessibility upgrades are overdue and should not be deferred again.
Protected cycle lanes are the single cheapest way to cut urban car trips.
Bike share schemes only work when docking stations are dense enough.
Cycling infrastructure is useless without secure parking at both ends.
Painted bike lanes without physical separation give a false sense of safety.
E-bike purchase subsidies would replace more car journeys than EV subsidies.
Congestion charges should vary by time of day and vehicle emissions.
Road pricing is fairer than fuel duty once most cars are electric.
Free parking in city centres is an enormous hidden subsidy to drivers.
Low-emission zones price poorer drivers out of their own city.
Revenue from road pricing must be ring-fenced for public transport.
Single-family zoning should be abolished in every major metropolitan area.
Upzoning near transit stations is the highest-value reform available.
Permitting delays add more to housing costs than construction materials do.
Allowing gentle density in suburbs beats building towers on the periphery.
Height limits in city centres protect views at the expense of housing.
Rent caps are a necessary emergency measure even if they distort supply.
Rent stabilisation should apply to older stock but exempt new construction.
Landlord licensing schemes improve conditions more than rent caps do.
Tenant right-to-buy schemes shrink the rental stock over time.
Longer default tenancies would give renters real security without price caps.
Social housing should be mixed into wealthy districts, not concentrated.
Councils should build homes directly rather than subsidise private developers.
Maintenance backlogs in public housing are a scandal that dwarfs new building.
Housing-first programmes are cheaper than the street homelessness they replace.
Public land should be leased for affordable homes rather than sold outright.
Whole-flat short-term lets should require a licence capped per neighbourhood.
Short-term rental platforms must hand over booking data to city regulators.
Banning short lets in tourist districts simply pushes them into the suburbs.
Home sharing while the owner is present is not the problem worth regulating.
Tourism levies on short lets should fund affordable housing directly.
Healthcare funded from general taxation is simpler than insurance mandates.
Private insurance top-ups undermine the solidarity of a universal system.
Waiting lists, not coverage, are the real failure of our health system.
Dental and optical care should be inside universal coverage, not outside it.
Co-payments deter exactly the patients who most need early treatment.
Governments should negotiate drug prices collectively across countries.
Publicly funded research should come with public licensing conditions.
Generic substitution should be automatic unless a doctor objects in writing.
Patent thickets on biologics keep prices high long after real innovation ends.
Price caps on essential medicines would not meaningfully slow drug discovery.
Mental health services deserve the same waiting-time guarantees as physical care.
School counsellors prevent far more crises than emergency psychiatric beds.
Talking therapies should be available without a psychiatric diagnosis first.
Crisis response should send trained clinicians rather than police officers.
Digital therapy apps are not a substitute for a human therapist.
Rural hospital closures are a public safety issue, not just an inconvenience.
Telemedicine cannot replace a local clinic when broadband itself is patchy.
Doctors trained at public expense should serve underserved regions first.
Ambulance response targets should be identical in rural and urban areas.
Community paramedics could cover much of what rural clinics no longer do.
Undergraduate tuition should be free at the point of use, funded by taxation.
Student loan interest above inflation turns education into a lifelong tax.
Income-contingent repayment is fairer than blanket loan forgiveness.
Debt forgiveness mostly benefits graduates who will earn well anyway.
Apprenticeships deserve the same public funding per head as degrees do.
Teacher salaries must track graduate wages or shortages will keep worsening.
Smaller class sizes matter less than having an experienced teacher in the room.
Classroom assistants are the cheapest way to raise attainment in early years.
Retention bonuses beat recruitment campaigns for fixing teacher shortages.
Teachers should be paid more to work in the most deprived schools.
Standardised testing narrows teaching to whatever the exam happens to measure.
Every secondary curriculum should include statistics and media literacy.
National exams give parents information they otherwise could not get.
Coursework assessment is fairer than a single high-stakes exam day.
Teaching a second language from age six pays off for the rest of life.
Selective admissions entrench advantage under the language of merit.
Charter and free schools drain the most engaged families from local schools.
Parents should be able to choose a school outside their catchment area.
Private school tax exemptions are indefensible while state schools ration books.
School choice without free transport is choice only for those with cars.
Border enforcement spending has grown without improving actual outcomes.
Employer sanctions do more to deter irregular migration than fences do.
Detention of migrant children cannot be justified under any circumstances.
Safe legal routes reduce smuggling more effectively than patrols do.
Countries have a right to control who crosses their borders.
Work visas should be tied to sectors with proven shortages, not to employers.
Tying a visa to one employer invites exploitation of migrant workers.
Seasonal agricultural visas need enforceable wage and housing standards.
Points-based systems undervalue care work that the economy actually needs.
Graduates trained here should get an automatic right to work here.
Asylum claims should be processed within six months or granted by default.
Offshore asylum processing outsources a legal duty we should meet ourselves.
Asylum seekers should be allowed to work while their claim is decided.
Resettlement quotas should be shared across regions, not left to a few cities.
Climate displacement will require a legal status that does not yet exist.
Free language courses are the highest-return integration spending available.
Recognition of foreign qualifications is where integration policy actually fails.
Citizenship tests full of trivia measure nothing about belonging.
Dispersal policies work only when housing and school places follow the people.
Local councils know integration needs better than national ministries do.
Consent banners have made privacy worse by turning it into a clicking chore.
Selling location data should be banned outright, not merely disclosed.
Data minimisation duties work better than user consent as a legal standard.
Privacy regulators are underfunded relative to the firms they supervise.
Encryption backdoors would endanger far more people than they protect.
AI systems used in hiring should be auditable by an outside regulator.
Training on copyrighted work without licensing is not fair use.
Safety rules should target high-risk deployments, not model size thresholds.
Public bodies should never make benefit decisions by automated system alone.
Open model weights make safety research possible and should be protected.
App store commissions of thirty percent are a tax on the whole software economy.
Interoperability mandates would do more for competition than breakups.
Acquisitions of small rivals by dominant platforms should be presumed illegal.
Self-preferencing in search results is the clearest antitrust harm to fix.
Breaking up large platforms would degrade the services people actually like.
Platforms should be liable for content they algorithmically amplify.
Moderation decisions need an appeals process with real human review.
Anonymity protects dissidents far more than it protects harassers.
Age verification schemes create honeypots of sensitive identity data.
Transparency reports are meaningless without independent researcher access.
Farm subsidies should pay for public goods rather than acreage owned.
Direct payments per hectare mostly enrich the largest landowners.
Support should shift towards young farmers entering the sector.
Subsidised crop insurance encourages planting on land that should be restored.
Food security justifies keeping some domestic production support in place.
A meat tax would be regressive without a matching cut on vegetables.
Public canteens should default to plant-based meals with meat on request.
Cultivated meat could cut emissions without asking anyone to change habits.
Livestock grazing maintains landscapes that arable farming would destroy.
Dairy alternatives should not be barred from using words like milk.
Front-of-pack traffic light labels change purchasing more than ingredient lists.
Country-of-origin labelling should be mandatory for all processed meat.
Pesticide residue limits should be set by public bodies, not industry panels.
Ultra-processed food warnings deserve the same footing as tobacco warnings.
Best-before dates cause enormous avoidable food waste in households.
Public procurement should favour food grown within the same region.
Farmers markets are charming but cannot feed a city on their own.
Urban allotments matter more for community than for actual food supply.
Short supply chains are more resilient than globally optimised ones.
Food co-operatives deserve the same tax treatment as supermarkets.
